Yes. The latest analysis detected **13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025**, equivalent to 3.91% of the property. The JRC 2020 reference classified 98% of the affected area as forest in 2020.

The event has not yet met the tool’s full corroboration rule because no later year has been observed. Tree-cover loss does not by itself establish the cause or whether the change is permanent.
